facts.fact: The MOU signed by the United States and Ethiopia sets a schedule for the national multi-tenant EMR: customisation and piloting in 2026, 48 facilities by 2027, a further 130 in each of 2028, 2029 and 2030, and 438 in total by 2030, with a costed, phased implementation plan still to be developed.

facts.fact: The US Government plans to support customising the national multi-tenant EMR and contribute to its roll-out from data-systems funding of US$18,850,149 over 2026-2030 shared across all the listed systems, while Ethiopia intends to pay licensing, cloud and hardware costs the US does not pay; the stated aim is to pass system support to government.

facts.fact: On 23 December 2025 Ethiopia and the United States signed an MOU, with activities from 1 April 2026 to 31 December 2030, under which the national multi-tenant EMR is to be customised and piloted in 2026 and rolled out to 438 facilities by 2030.
facts.system: comprehensive multi-tenant open source Electronic Medical Records (EMR)

facts.fact: The MOU's 2030 vision names District Health Information System 2 as Ethiopia's Health Management Information System within an integrated, interoperable health data system, and uses DHIS2 as the data source for most of its outcome and process metrics; it sets no roll-out target for DHIS2.

The US Government plans to provide comprehensive HMIS/DHIS2 support as strategic assistance and US$18,850,149 of data-systems funding over 2026-2030 across all the listed systems, while Ethiopia intends to pay ongoing licensing, cloud and hardware costs the US does not pay.
